package planted

import (
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// ── vacuous-loop: WANT ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// TestVacuousDiscovery is the reliant TestProjectWorkflows_* shape: a checkout
// leaves the directory present but EMPTY, the loop runs zero times, and the
// test reports green having asserted nothing.
func TestVacuousDiscovery(t *testing.T) {
	entries, err := os.ReadDir("fixtures")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadDir: %v", err)
	}
	for _, e := range entries {
		t.Run(e.Name(), func(t *testing.T) {
			b, rerr := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("fixtures", e.Name(), "want.json"))
			if rerr != nil {
				t.Fatalf("read golden: %v", rerr)
			}
			if len(b) == 0 {
				t.Error("golden is empty")
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestVacuousGlob is the same shape through filepath.Glob.
func TestVacuousGlob(t *testing.T) {
	files, _ := filepath.Glob("testdata/*.golden")
	for _, f := range files {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(f)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", f, err)
		}
		if len(b) == 0 {
			t.Errorf("%s is empty", f)
		}
	}
}

// ── vacuous-loop: must NOT fire ──────────────────────────────────────────────

// TestGuardedByLen proves the set was non-empty before trusting the loop.
func TestGuardedByLen(t *testing.T) {
	entries, err := os.ReadDir("fixtures")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadDir: %v", err)
	}
	if len(entries) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no fixtures discovered — the corpus is missing, which is a failure, not a pass")
	}
	for _, e := range entries {
		if e.Name() == "" {
			t.Errorf("empty name")
		}
	}
}

// TestGuardedByWitness proves it with a flag the loop sets, transitively
// through a second loop — the shape add_entity_from_proto_test really uses.
func TestGuardedByWitness(t *testing.T) {
	entries, _ := os.ReadDir("db/migrations")
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, e := range entries {
		seen[e.Name()] = true
	}
	found := false
	for name := range seen {
		if name == "001_create_users.up.sql" {
			found = true
		}
	}
	if !found {
		t.Error("migration not born")
	}
}

// TestGuardedByCounter proves it with a COUNTER the loop bumps and the test
// compares after it. Same proof as TestGuardedByWitness, spelled the way a
// test that filters the discovered set has to spell it: `found := false` says
// "at least one", `checked != 3` says "exactly the three I expect", and only
// the second one can catch a scaffold that stopped emitting one of them.
//
// The bump is `checked++`, an IncDecStmt — not an AssignStmt. A closure that
// walked only assignments never saw the counter become a witness and flagged
// this shape, which is how scaffold_test_split_test.go came up red.
func TestGuardedByCounter(t *testing.T) {
	entries, _ := os.ReadDir("internal/handlers/admin")
	checked := 0
	for _, e := range entries {
		if !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), "_test.go") {
			continue
		}
		checked++
		if e.Name() == "" {
			t.Errorf("empty name")
		}
	}
	if checked != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("checked %d scaffold tests, want 3", checked)
	}
}

// TestAssertsEmptiness ranges to prove the set is EMPTY. Vacuity is the pass
// condition here, so demanding a non-empty proof would be backwards.
func TestAssertsEmptiness(t *testing.T) {
	if entries, err := os.ReadDir("proto/services"); err == nil {
		for _, e := range entries {
			if e.IsDir() {
				t.Fatalf("zero-service scaffold grew a service dir %s", e.Name())
			}
		}
	}
}

// ── dead-skip: WANT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// TestSkipOnRepoFixture skips when a file tracked in this repository is
// missing. It can never fire on a checkout — until someone renames the file,
// at which point the test evaporates instead of failing.
func TestSkipOnRepoFixture(t *testing.T) {
	kclRoot, _ := filepath.Abs("../../kcl")
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(kclRoot, "schema.k")); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("forge kcl module not found at %s: %v", kclRoot, err)
	}
	t.Log("render")
}

// TestPermanentlySkipped can never run.
func TestPermanentlySkipped(t *testing.T) {
	t.Skip("fixture wires via a retired path; re-author against the new one")
	t.Log("unreachable")
}

// ── dead-skip: must NOT fire ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

// TestSkipOnMissingToolchain is legitimate: no checkout can supply kcl.
func TestSkipOnMissingToolchain(t *testing.T) {
	if !toolAvailable("kcl") {
		t.Skip("kcl not on PATH")
	}
}

// TestSkipOnShort is legitimate.
func TestSkipOnShort(t *testing.T) {
	if testing.Short() {
		t.Skip("boots real postgres; skipped under -short")
	}
}

// TestSkipOnPlatform is legitimate.
func TestSkipOnPlatform(t *testing.T) {
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
		t.Skip("unix-only signal model")
	}
}

// TestSkipOnSiblingCheckout is legitimate: the path is derived from the
// environment, so it is genuinely outside this repository.
func TestSkipOnSiblingCheckout(t *testing.T) {
	dir := os.Getenv("CPFORGE_PROJECT_DIR")
	if dir == "" {
		dir = filepath.Join(os.Getenv("HOME"), "src/reliant-labs/cp-forge")
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(dir + "/deploy/kcl/dev"); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("cp-forge not present: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestSkipOnMissingHome is legitimate: a container may have no HOME.
func TestSkipOnMissingHome(t *testing.T) {
	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil || home == "" {
		t.Skip("no home dir")
	}
}

// ── silent-capability: WANT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

// TestCapabilityGuardedLint is the exact shape forge shipped five times: the
// only lint gate the test has, wrapped in "if the tool happens to be here".
// On a box without it the assertion does not weaken, it VANISHES, and the
// function still reports PASS. The t.Log else-branch is what makes it look
// deliberate.
func TestCapabilityGuardedLint(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	runCmd(t, dir, "go", "build", "./...")
	if toolAvailable("golangci-lint") {
		runCmd(t, dir, "golangci-lint", "run", "./...")
	} else {
		t.Log("golangci-lint not available, skipping lint check")
	}
}

// TestCapabilityBailsMidTest is the same defect wearing the other hat: a bare
// return that drops npm install + build + test + typecheck — the most expensive
// and most load-bearing half of the test — and reports PASS.
func TestCapabilityBailsMidTest(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	if !toolAvailable("node") || !toolAvailable("npm") {
		t.Log("node/npm not available — skipping npm build gate (content assertions still ran)")
		return
	}
	runCmd(t, dir, "npm", "install")
	runCmd(t, dir, "npm", "run", "build")
}

// TestLookPathGuardedWork writes the probe inline instead of through a helper.
// The rule must see through the two-line spelling, or renaming the helper is
// all it takes to go blind.
func TestLookPathGuardedWork(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	if _, err := exec.LookPath("kcl"); err == nil {
		runCmd(t, dir, "kcl", "run", "main.k")
	}
}

// ── silent-capability: must NOT fire ─────────────────────────────────────────

// TestProbeThenSkip is honest: the machine's gap is reported, so a reader of
// the run knows the gate did not happen. (TestSkipOnMissingToolchain above is
// the same shape and is named separately by the dead-skip fixtures.)
func TestProbeThenSkip(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	if !toolAvailable("kcl") {
		t.Skipf("kcl not on PATH — the render gate cannot run")
	}
	runCmd(t, dir, "kcl", "run", "main.k")
}

// TestProbeThenFail is honest the other way: this repository's CI provisions
// kcl, so its absence is a broken job, not a property of the machine.
func TestProbeThenFail(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	if !toolAvailable("kcl") {
		t.Fatalf("kcl not on PATH — CI must provision it")
	}
	runCmd(t, dir, "kcl", "run", "main.k")
}

// TestProbeIsBookkeeping collects what is missing on the way to ONE decision.
// Both outcomes verify exactly as much (nothing); flagging this would flag
// every helper that builds a list before judging it, and a rule that flags
// requireTool itself is a rule nobody keeps.
func TestProbeIsBookkeeping(t *testing.T) {
	var missing []string
	for _, name := range []string{"node", "npm"} {
		if _, err := exec.LookPath(name); err != nil {
			missing = append(missing, name)
		}
	}
	if len(missing) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("missing: %s", strings.Join(missing, ", "))
	}
}

// TestProbeChoosesBetweenTwoRealPaths is a genuine either/or: both branches
// verify the same claim, one through each package manager. Nothing is lost by
// taking either, which is the one honest use of a capability boolean.
func TestProbeChoosesBetweenTwoRealPaths(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	if toolAvailable("pnpm") {
		runCmd(t, dir, "pnpm", "install")
	} else {
		runCmd(t, dir, "npm", "install")
	}
}

// TestNonProbeConditional asserts a bad substring is absent. The body is
// nothing but a failure, the condition is not a tool probe, and this is the
// single most common shape in the repository — flagging it would end the rule.
func TestNonProbeConditional(t *testing.T) {
	content := "package main"
	if strings.Contains(content, "TODO: implement") {
		t.Errorf("scaffold shipped a placeholder: %s", content)
	}
}

func toolAvailable(string) bool { return false }

func runCmd(*testing.T, string, string, ...string) {}
